name: Variational World Model
analogy: Think of it as a weather forecaster for the market who never says just one thing will happen. Given today's chart, the forecaster describes a cloud of plausible next bars, wide on jumpy days and tight on quiet ones, and can draw you as many sample days from that cloud as you like.

steps.title: Compress the bar into a spread, not a point
steps.description: An encoder reads a bar and outputs a small distribution for its hidden state: a centre and a width for each number. The width says how unsure the model is about what the bar really means.
steps.inExample: The 10:15 five-minute MNQ bar is encoded into 12 hidden numbers, each with a centre and a width.

steps.title: Sample a hidden state from that spread
steps.description: A single hidden state is drawn at random from the spread, in a way that still lets learning flow back through the draw. Each draw is one plausible reading of the bar.
steps.inExample: One draw gives a hidden state that reads the bar as an orderly advance on moderate volume.

steps.title: Predict the next hidden state from history alone
steps.description: A learned prior, using only the past and the action, gives a spread for where the hidden state goes next. This is the forward prediction, and it is a whole distribution, not one value.
steps.inExample: The prior says the next state is probably another orderly advance, with a smaller chance of a sharp reversal.

steps.title: Rebuild the bar from the hidden state
steps.description: A decoder turns a hidden state back into bar features and a reward estimate. Training asks for good rebuilding while keeping the encoder's spread close to the prior, which is what keeps the picture honest.
steps.inExample: The decoder rebuilds the bar's range and volume from the hidden draw and estimates the net result of the last action.

steps.title: Train on a balance of fit and honesty
steps.description: The two demands are combined into one score: rebuild well, but do not let the encoder claim more certainty than the history allows. This helps keep the predicted widths calibrated.
steps.inExample: On held-out folds, the check is whether about 80 percent of real next-bar moves fall inside the model's stated 80 percent range.

steps.title: Sample many futures to see the range
steps.description: To look ahead, the model draws many hidden-state paths from the prior, decodes each one and collects the outcomes. The spread of those outcomes is the forecast, including its tails.
steps.inExample: From the 10:15 bar, 500 imagined 6-bar paths are drawn and decoded into price moves.

useFor.example: Holding 1 MNQ contract when the imagined 6-bar outcomes are wide and 3 when they are tight.
Sampling 500 imagined 6-bar paths to see how often a 40-point stop would be hit.
Using the full set of imagined outcomes to evaluate a rule that exits at a target or a stop, whichever comes first.
Producing a 6-bar range forecast on ES and checking it against realized ranges in walk-forward folds.
Treating a bar the model rebuilds poorly, or one that falls in its far tail, as a sign of unusual conditions.

avoidWhen: A single direction call is the whole need; a classifier is simpler and its probability is easier to evaluate.
The tails matter and data on them is thin; the model's tails are only as good as the few extreme bars it saw, and may look reassuringly narrow.

example.scenario: At 10:15 on an MNQ session the model draws 500 imagined 6-bar futures to give a position-sizing range for the next 30 minutes.

input.summary: The current bar's features and the action the agent is considering.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The close of the 10:15 five-minute bar, rounded to a whole point.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent five-minute bar.

fields.name: volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: How heavy trading in this bar was compared with the recent norm.

fields.name: return over the last 6 bars
fields.value: up about a fifth of one percent
fields.meaning: How much price has risen over the previous 30 minutes.

fields.name: imagined paths requested
fields.meaning: How many sampled futures the model is asked to produce.

fields.name: median imagined move
fields.meaning: The middle outcome across the 500 imagined paths.

fields.name: 10th percentile of imagined moves
fields.meaning: One tenth of imagined paths ended lower than this.

fields.name: 90th percentile of imagined moves
fields.meaning: One tenth of imagined paths ended higher than this.

fields.name: chance an imagined path touches a 30-point stop
fields.meaning: The share of paths that moved 30 points against a long position at some point.

example.reading: The median is small relative to a spread of about 90 points, so size should be set by the spread, not the lean. Check calibration first: if real outcomes fall outside the stated 10th-to-90th range far more than 20 percent of the time, shrink your trust in the tails.
